rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ promise to inform them concerns hidden household facts—what they ate and stored—so the coordinated acts are miracles, since informing concerns concealed matters.
rows.anchor: لتكون هاته المتعاطفات كلها من قبيل المعجزات بقرينة قوله أنبئكم لأن الإنباء يكون في الأمور الخفية

words: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miracles are signs inviting belief if the Israelites wish to believe; the address confronts people who met Jesus’ call with denial and insults.
rows.anchor: جعل هذه الأشياء كلها آيات تدعو إلى الإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an indirectly rebuts Christians who infer Jesus’ divinity from acts beyond human power; that argument is sophistical, and the wording attributes the acts to God’s permission.
rows.anchor: فمن قدر عليها فهو الإله

rows.speaker: أهل السير
rows.claim: Historians report that the Christians of Najran used these miracles as an argument before the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أهل السير أن نصارى نجران استدلوا بهذه الأعمال لدى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited poetic verse, the main purpose is boasting that the group die in battle by the sword; the poet then presents this as a habitual trait, not exaggeration.
rows.anchor: فإن الغرض الأهم هو التمدح بأنهم يقتلون في الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shayʾan” can be the object of “tushrikū”: make nothing worshipped a partner, as in the cited verse from al-Jinn.
rows.anchor: أي لا تجعلوا شريكا شيئا مما يعبد كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “shayʾan” is an emphatic cognate accusative: do not commit shirk at all, even a slight amount, as in the cited verse from al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: ويجوز انتصابه على المصدرية للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the command to treat parents well immediately after worship emphasizes their status; the author links the order to the commands in Luqman.
rows.anchor: اهتمام بشأن الوالدين إذ جعل الأمر بالإحسان إليهما عقب الأمر بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object governed by “iḥsānan” is brought forward for emphasis, not restriction, because benevolence is prescribed toward everything.
rows.anchor: ولذا قدم معمول ( إحسانا ) عليه تقديما للاهتمام إذ لا معنى للحصر هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun “iḥsānan” stands in place of a verb.
rows.anchor: ووقع المصدر موقع الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “iḥsān” takes the preposition bāʾ because it includes the sense of birr: respectful treatment and honoring a person; financial benefit instead takes ilā.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن الإحسان إنما يعدى بالباء إذا أريد به الإحسان المتعلق بمعاملة الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphans and the poor are singled out for care because both groups are weak and lack anyone to support them.
rows.anchor: هذان صنفان ضعيفان عديما النصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near-related neighbor is a neighbor belonging to one’s tribe; the distant neighbor is a stranger who has settled among the tribe.
rows.anchor: الجار النسيب من القبيلة ، وب { الجار الجنب } الجار الغريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Al-junub” means distant, from janib (“side”); Ibn ʿAshur analyzes it as an adjective on faʿl, while noting a competing verbal-noun analysis.
rows.anchor: فهو جنب ، أي بعيد ، مشتق من الجانب ، وهو وصف على وزن فعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take “junub” as a verbal noun, which explains why it does not agree in form with the word it describes.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو مصدر ، ولذلك لم يطابق موصوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by Balaʿa ibn Qays contrasts a relative neighbor with a strange, non-tribal neighbor, supporting Ibn ʿAshur’s interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال بلعاء بن قيس : لا يجتوينا مجاور أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada’s phrase “from estrangement” likewise uses janāba for being a stranger or outsider.
rows.anchor: ويشهد لهذا المعنى قول علقمة بن عبدة في شعره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the near and distant neighbors as those close to or far from one’s home; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this because qurba is not used for spatial proximity.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد ، لأن القربى لا تعرف في القرب المكاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam reinforces the Arabs’ established virtue of honoring neighbors and completes their noble character by commanding kindness to them.
rows.anchor: والعرب معروفون بحفظ الجوار والإحسان إلى الجار

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet said Gabriel kept advising him about the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would be made an heir; al-Bukhari records it.
rows.anchor: ففي ( البخاري ) عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو شريح
rows.claim: Abu Shurayh reports the Prophet’s repeated oath that a person whose neighbor is not safe from his harms does not truly believe; al-Bukhari records it.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن أبي شريح : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج وهو يقول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asked which of her two neighbors should receive a gift, and the Prophet told her to choose the one whose door was nearer; al-Bukhari records it.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن عائشة ، قلت : ( يا رسول الله إن لي جارين

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr to add water to broth and share it considerately with his neighbors; Muslim records the report.
rows.anchor: وفي ( صحيح مسلم ) : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب والأوزاعي
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab and al-Awzaʿi define the neighbor’s range as forty houses in every direction; a hadith is also reported for this limit.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن شهاب ، والأوزاعي : أربعون دارا من كل ناحية

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: No fixed boundary for neighborliness is transmitted from Malik.
rows.anchor: وليس عن مالك في ذلك حد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scope of neighborliness is best left to what people customarily recognize.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه موكول إلى ما تعارفه الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion at one’s side is someone who stays nearby: a guest, a travel companion, or anyone visiting in hope of receiving help.
rows.anchor: هو المصاحب الملازم للمكان ، فمنه الضيف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies the companion at one’s side as one’s wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد الزوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ibn al-sabīl” is a traveler passing through without intending to settle; “ibn” conveys association, and the road is imagined to have cast him toward the people as its child.
rows.anchor: فابن السبيل هو الذي لازم الطريق سائرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traveler merits care because he is vulnerable, has few supporters, and cannot readily learn the circumstances of an unfamiliar people and place.
rows.anchor: والوصاية به لأنه ضعيف الحيلة ، قليل النصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enslaved people merit special care because slavery leaves them needy and weak, with their masters blocking routes to freedom.
rows.anchor: لأن العبيد في ضعف الرق والحاجة وانقطاع سبل الخلاص من سادتهم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالًۭا فَخُورًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause is a summative censure of traits that commonly obstruct kindness to the named groups.
rows.anchor: تذييل لجملة الأمر بالإحسان إلى من سماهم بذم موانع الإحسان إليهم الغالبة على البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtiyāl is arrogance, derived from khuyalāʾ; fakhūr is someone intensely boastful about what he has done.
rows.anchor: والاختيال : التكبر ، افتعال مشتق من الخيلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both traits produce harshness and rudeness, opposed to the commanded kindness and to humility toward people thought unable to retaliate.
rows.anchor: وكلا الوصفين منشأ للغلظة والجفاء ، فهما ينافيان الإحسان المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s lack of love here means withholding approval and nearness from the person described.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نفي محبة الله تعالى نفي رضاه وتقريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The censure alludes to the roughness and harshness associated with polytheists and warns believers against retaining those former traits.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعريض بأخلاق أهل الشرك ، لما عرفوا به من الغلطة والجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward exceeds a simple doubling; “from Himself” is an honorific attribution, and it is called reward because it recompenses good work.
rows.anchor: والأجر العظيم ما يزاد على الضعف ، ولذلك أضافه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: An unspecified report says this verse was revealed concerning the reward for emigration.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن هذا نزل في ثواب الهجرة

words: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial fāʾ may be explanatory, with an omitted condition prompted by the preceding threat, rebuke, and promise: once convinced of them, consider the scene when witnesses come.
rows.anchor: الفاء يجوز أن تكون فاء فصيحة تدل على شرط مقدر

words: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fāʾ derives the question from God’s assurance that He does no injustice: people will divide between joy and regret when witnesses arrive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع على قوله : { إن الله لا يظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second parsing, direct address replaces an explicit reference to the Messenger as witness over the community, honoring him by giving him the dignity of direct presence.
rows.anchor: فعدل إلى الخطاب تشريفا للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بعز الحضور والإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question evokes a terrifying scene for the polytheists: seeing witnesses proves they were warned and leaves them bewildered as they try to escape punishment.
rows.anchor: والحالة التي دل عليها الاستفهام المستعمل في التعجيب تؤذن بحالة مهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question’s omitted subject is something like “how will those people be?” or “how will the scene be?”; it is not limited to one state because saved and doomed people see contrasting outcomes.
rows.anchor: ولذلك حذف المبتدأ المستفهم عنه ويقدر بنحو : كيف أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness is given no explicit complement meaning “for” or “against,” so the wording includes testimony in either direction.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لما ذكر الشهيد لم يذكر معه متعلقه بعلى أو اللام : ليعم الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is used for amazement, as in the similar construction at 3:25.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في لازم معناه من التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is a clarifying restart: it answers the listener’s question about the strange situation raised by “how?” by showing the disbelievers’ terror when witnesses’ testimony and punishment become clear.
rows.anchor: الآية استئناف بياني ، لأن السامع يتساءل عن الحالة المبهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause explains what they wish for; its content functions like the object of “yود,” with “law” functioning as a nominalizing particle.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لو تسوى بهم الأرض } بيان لجملة يود أي يودون ودا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the tāʾ open and the sīn doubled: the form is the imperfect of tasawwā, the passive counterpart of making something equal, with two tāʾs assimilated.
rows.anchor: قرأه نافع ، وابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر بفتح التاء وتشديد السين

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use an open tāʾ and undoubled sīn, retaining the same meaning as the previous reading while deleting one tāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بفتح التاء وتخفيف السين

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use a damma on the tāʾ and a light sīn, making the verb passive: the earth would be made equal with them.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير ، وابن عامر ، وأبو عمرو ، ويعقوب { تسوى } بضم التاء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand the wish as becoming earth themselves; the wording elaborates by indirect allusion to their becoming dust, like 78:40.
rows.anchor: وهذا تفسير الجمهور ، وعلى هذا فالكلام إطناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ziyad al-Aʿjam’s line about generosity, manliness, and giving being beneath Ibn al-Ḥashraj’s tent illustrates an indirect attribution of those virtues to the person.
rows.anchor: إن السماحة والمروءة والندى في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One proposed interpretation is that they wish not to be resurrected, remaining level with the earth inside it.
rows.anchor: فقيل : يودون أنهم لم يبعثوا وبقوا مستوين مع الأرض في بطنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another proposed interpretation is that they wish to be buried again, as they had been before resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يودون أن يدفنوا حينئذ كما كانوا قبل البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is that the earth rise to the same level as their bodies, hiding them; this conveys their terror and humiliation as they shrink from view.
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي : أن المعنى التسوية في البروز والظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation best fits the indirect allusion; a Bedouin’s satire of Tayyiʾ, as quoted by al-Mubarrad, pictures people becoming indistinguishable.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن في معنى الآية وأنسب بالكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be an independent sentence coordinated with “they wish,” sharing its subject.
rows.anchor: والواو عاطفة لها على جملة { يود }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial clause: they wish the earth would cover them while they are unable to conceal anything from God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون حالية ، أي يودون لو تسوى بهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing earlier nations’ witnesses and consequences, they expect their own turn and want to hide; they can neither confess the ruinous truth nor risk concealment, so they wish to disappear.
rows.anchor: علموا أن النوبة مفضية إليهم ، وخامرهم أن يكتموا الله أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes to explain two prayer rulings; the contemporaneous need to regulate wine placed this ruling between surrounding verses, apparently interrupting their sequence when the occasion arose.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية استئناف لبيان حكمين يتعلقان بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine was still originally lawful and some Muslims drank it; after 2:219 some argued they drank for its benefits rather than its sin, while the verse signaled likely prohibition and prepared them for it without yet removing the allowance.
rows.anchor: ونزل قوله تعالى : { يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس } ( البقرة : 219 )

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf served food and wine; when Ali led prayer while intoxicated, he recited al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, and this verse was revealed. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : صنع لنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “approach” is metaphorical for engaging in an act; literally, qaruba or qaribahu means to be near a place or person, and both forms have the same sense.
rows.anchor: والقرب هنا مستعمل في معناه المجازي وهو التلبس بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish the kasra form as exclusively metaphorical, but Ibn ʿAshur says that distinction is incorrect.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن مكسور الراء للقرب المجازي خاصة ، ولا يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing “do not approach prayer” instead of “do not pray” presents intoxication as incompatible with prayer and the drinker as unworthy of Islam’s best act, discouraging wine and signaling a change in its status.
rows.anchor: وإنما اختير هذا الفعل دون لا تصلوا ونحوه للإشارة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take “prayer” to mean the mosque by naming the place for the state; Ibn ʿAshur calls this far-fetched and contrary to well-known reports.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من تأول الصلاة هنا بالمسجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن
rows.claim: They report that some Companions drank wine and then came to the mosque to pray with the Prophet, prompting this prohibition; Ibn ʿAshur says this conflicts with the well-known reports.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عباس ، وابن مسعود ، والحسن قالوا : كان جماعة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Until you know what you say” gives the prohibition’s limit and hints at its rationale; impaired speech signals the earlier disruption of prayer’s actions as reason fails.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { حتى تعلموا ما تقولون } غاية للنهي وإيماء إلى علته

words: وَأَنتُمْ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمُوا۟ مَا تَقُولُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may imply that mild intoxication did not then bar prayer; alternatively, the limit may mean the end of drunkenness, after which some exhilaration remains.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إيذان بأن السكر الخفيف لا يمنع الصلاة يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sukārā” is the plural of sakrān, whose reason is closed or blocked, as when a pool or door is shut; compare the eyes being obscured in 15:15.
rows.anchor: وسكارى جمع سكران ، والسكران من أخذ عقله في الانغلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After revelation, Muslims avoided wine around prayer, drinking only after the night prayer or after dawn prayer because of the long intervals; the later rule also prohibited prayer without purification.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية اجتنب المسلمون شرب الخمر في أوقات الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Wa-lā junuban” is coordinated with the circumstantial clause “while you are intoxicated”; its accusative form confirms that the circumstantial clause occupies an accusative position.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وأنتم سكارى } لأنا في محل الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Junub may be a verbal noun or an adjective like ajadd; here it means being distant from prayer and worship after intercourse until bathing, as at 4:36.
rows.anchor: والجنب فعل ، قيل : مصدر ، وقيل : وصف مثل أجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a verbal-noun adjective, junub does not take a plural form even though it describes a plural subject.
rows.anchor: ووصف جنب وصف بالمصدر فلذلك لم يجمع إذ أخبر به عن جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to avoid prayer while in janāba means not to pray until one has performed the ritual bath.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا تصلوا في حال الجنابة حتى تغتسلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term and ritual bath were known before Islam, perhaps inherited from ḥanīf practice or borrowed from Jews.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الجنابة على هذا المعنى من عهد الجاهلية ، فإن الاغتسال من الجنابة كان معروفا عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur says he has not found Arabic usage evidencing mention of ritual bathing from janāba.
rows.anchor: ولم أقف على شيء من كلام العرب يدل على ذكر غسل الجنابة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq’s Sīra says Abū Sufyān, returning defeated from Badr, swore not to touch his head with the bath of janāba until he fought Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن إسحاق في ( السيرة ) أن أبا سفيان ، لما رجع مهزوما من بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of janāba is an embedded transition to the new rule of tayammum, since the requirement of ritual bathing was already established.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من قوله : { ولا جنبا } التمهيد للتخلص إلى شرع التيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum was instituted during the campaign of al-Muraysīʿ, in either year five or six AH according to the preferred chronology.
rows.anchor: والتيمم شرع في غزوة المريسيع على الصحيح ، وكانت سنة ست أو سنة خمس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from Malik via Aisha says the tayammum verse was revealed at al-Muraysīʿ; Ibn ʿAshur infers this likely means the Nisa verse, since its discussion there mentions only tayammum.
rows.anchor: وظاهر حديث مالك عن عائشة أن الآية التي نزلت في غزوة المريسيع هي آية التيمم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿAmr via Aisha, recorded by al-Bukhari, identifies the verse revealed at al-Muraysīʿ as the tayammum instruction in al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: ووقع في حديث عمرو عن عائشة أن الآية التي نزلت هي قوله :

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī firmly identifies the verse revealed at al-Muraysīʿ as this verse in al-Nisa, since al-Maʾida’s verse is called the verse of ablution.
rows.anchor: وقد جزم القرطبي بأن الآية التي نزلت في غزوة المريسيع هي آية سورة النساء

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī places Aisha’s report about the occasion of revelation under the Nisa verse in his Asbāb al-nuzūl.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الواحدي أورد في أسباب النزول حديث عائشة في سبب نزول آية سورة النساء

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls this a difficult problem without a solution, since it is unclear which of the two verses Aisha intended.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي هذه معضلة ما وجدت لدائها من دواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the order of al-Nisa and al-Maʾida is disputed, Ibn ʿAshur prefers the view that al-Nisa was revealed first.
rows.anchor: والأصح أن سورة النساء نزلت قبل سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is taken from the general set of circumstances implied by “junub,” an indefinite circumstantial phrase under a negation.
rows.anchor: استثناء من عموم الأحوال المستفاد من وقوع ( جنبا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a traveler while on a journey is an “ʿābir al-sabīl,” from crossing or passing through a river or road.
rows.anchor: وعابر السبيل ، في كلام العرب : المسافر حين سيره في سفره

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars understand “passing through” as passing through a mosque, on the premise that “prayer” means mosque; the exception then permits a junub person to cross without staying.
rows.anchor: ومن العلماء من فسر { عابري سبيل } بمارين في طريق ، وقال : المراد منه طريق المسجد

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وأبو عبيدة وابن المسيب والضحاك وعطاء ومجاهد ومسروق والنخعي وزيد بن أسلم وعمرو بن دينار وعكرمة وابن شهاب وقتادة
rows.claim: These authorities are reported to say the mosque-passage license belonged to an early period when many Emigrants and Helpers had doors opening into the mosque; it was later superseded after the doors were closed except Abū Bakr’s wicket, with reports also naming the Prophet and Abū Bakr, or ʿAlī, as exceptions.
rows.anchor: ونسب أيضا إلى أنس بن مالك ، وأبي عبيدة ، وابن المسيب ، والضحاك ، وعطاء ، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A claim that ʿAlī’s daughter’s wicket remained in the mosque is also reported, but Ibn ʿAshur says it is unsound.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أبقيت خوخة بنت علي في المسجد ، ولم يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who read prayer as the mosque and travelers as passers through it, the exception clearly removes passers-by from the general prohibition on a junub person’s states.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذا الاستثناء عند من فسر { تقربوا الصلاة } بدخول المسجد ، وفسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the majority’s literal reading, the exception seems redundant beside the later mention of travel and the restriction of the general rule; Ibn ʿAshur says it is placed here because travel commonly prevents bathing when water must be conserved, while illness is rarer.
rows.anchor: وأما عند الجمهور الذين حملوا الآية على ظاهرها في معنى تقربوا الصلاة ، وفي معنى عابري السبيل فلا تظهر له فائدة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats tayammum as a necessity-based permission, not removal of ritual impurity: a person who tayammums remains junub and may pray only as necessity permits, so the exception is connected.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الشافعي ، فهو عنده بدل ضروري يقدر بقدر الضرورة ، ودليله ظاهر الاستثناء

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa treats tayammum as removing ritual impurity until invalidated, so the exception is disconnected; after tayammum for janāba, a later nullifier requires wudu. Ibn ʿAshur calls this the apparent view, with no Sunna evidence against it.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي حنيفة ، فلذلك إذا تيمم الجنب وصلى وصار منه حدث ناقض للوضوء يتوضأ

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The well-known transmission from Ibn al-Qāsim says tayammum permits prayer without removing impurity, so each tayammum covers only one obligatory prayer; after a nullifier following tayammum for janāba, one tayammums again for wudu.
rows.anchor: فالمشهور من رواية ابن القاسم أن التيمم مبيح للصلاة وليس رافعا للحدث

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: In the Baghdadi transmission, a patient unable to use water may perform multiple prayers with one tayammum until a nullifier; this also applies to missed prayers, and no Malik report addresses a junub person who then loses wudu.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك ، في رواية البغداديين : أن المريض الذي لا يقدر على مس الماء يتيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among scholars who use legal implications, the unqualified traveler exception is further limited by “if you find no water”; the general prohibition on junub people is otherwise narrowed by the later illness-or-travel condition.
rows.anchor: وفي مفهوم هذا الاستثناء ، عند القائلين بالمفاهيم من الجمهور ، على هذا المحمل تفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Muslims already understood that prayer may occur without purification, the traveler exception awaits clarification and the following conditions clarify it; otherwise, those conditions introduce tayammum rules anew.
rows.anchor: ثم إن كان قد تقرر عند المسلمين أن الصلاة تقع بدون طهارة يبق قوله : { إلا عابري سبيل } مجملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is placed before the statement’s restriction is complete, an uncommon order used for emphasis, as illustrated by a line from Musa ibn Jabir al-Hanafi al-Umawi.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المستثنى في قوله : { إلا عابري سبيل } قبل تمام الكلام المقصود قصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line by Musa ibn Jabir al-Hanafi al-Umawi exemplifies placing the exception early for emphasis.
rows.anchor: كقول موسى بن جابر الحنفي أموي : لا أشتهي يا قوم إلا كارها
